title: The marginal vector field of a dataset
goal:
Implement Equation 8 for a finite dataset and the OT conditional path. With $q$ the empirical distribution on points $x_1^{(1)}, \dots, x_1^{(N)}$, the marginal field is

$$u_t(x) = \sum_i w_i(x, t)\, u_t(x \mid x_1^{(i)}), \qquad w_i(x, t) = \frac{p_t(x \mid x_1^{(i)})}{\sum_j p_t(x \mid x_1^{(j)})},$$

where $p_t(x \mid x_1) = \mathcal{N}(x \mid t\,x_1, \sigma_t^2 I)$ with $\sigma_t = 1 - (1 - \sigma_{\min})\,t$ (Equation 20) and $u_t(x \mid x_1) = \frac{x_1 - (1 - \sigma_{\min})\,x}{\sigma_t}$ (Equation 21).

Write `marginal_vf(x, t, data, sigma_min)`. `x` has shape `(n, d)`, `t` is a float in $[0, 1]$, and `data` has shape `(N, d)`. It returns shape `(n, d)`. This is the vector field that a perfectly flexible model reaches when it minimizes the CFM loss on this dataset (Theorem 2).

The tests check the continuity equation (Appendix B, Equation 26), so a wrong weighting fails even when the output has the right shape.
hints: The weights are a softmax over $i$ of $-\lVert x - t\,x_1^{(i)}\rVert^2 / (2\sigma_t^2)$. The normalizing constants of the Gaussians are equal across $i$, so they cancel.
Each Gaussian is centered at $t\,x_1^{(i)}$, not at $x_1^{(i)}$. At $t = 0$ every center is the origin, so every weight is equal.
Subtract the largest log-weight in each row before you exponentiate. Near $t = 1$ the variance $\sigma_t^2$ is tiny, and a plain `np.exp` underflows to $0 / 0$.
Build an array of shape `(n, N, d)` with `x[:, None, :]` and `data[None]`, then sum over axis 1.
